The scenario: Defendant Xiao, after work injury compensation denied, brings a gas cylinder and lighter to an office, opens gas valve, then lights lighter then extinguishes, then after persuasion he stops, lets victims leave. He waited at scene, was arrested, no resistance. So what crime? Possibly "放火" (arson) or "非法使用易燃易爆物品"? In Chinese criminal law, setting fire or causing explosion is arson. However he did not actually cause fire, just opened gas valve and lit but extinguished, no damage. Could be "危害公共安全罪" (endangering public safety) maybe "放火罪" requires actual fire. There's also "非法点燃易燃气体罪"? Not typical. Could be "非法使用危险物质罪"? Let's recall Chinese criminal law: Article 115 (放火罪) requires setting fire causing damage. If no fire, maybe "非法制造、买卖、运输、储存、使用危险物质罪"? Actually there is "危险物品肇事罪"? Not sure.

But similar example: earlier example about setting fire to house: they labeled "放火". That case had actual fire causing property loss. Here no fire, just attempted arson? Could be "未遂放火罪" (attempted arson). In Chinese classification, attempted crimes are still the same name with "未遂". The answer likely "放火未遂". However examples didn't include "未遂" suffix; they just gave base crime. For example, earlier example about "故意伤害;故意毁坏财物" they didn't add "未遂". So maybe just "放火". But need to see if there is a specific crime "非法点燃易燃气体" not typical.

Check Chinese criminal law: Article 115: "放火罪" includes "以燃烧、爆炸等手段危害公共安全". If no fire, maybe "以危险方法危害公共安全罪" (dangerous means). There's Article 115 also includes "以燃放烟花爆竹、燃放鞭炮、使用易燃易爆物品等方式危害公共安全". Actually there is Article 115: "以燃烧、爆炸等手段危害公共安全的，处三年以上七年以下有期徒刑". So even if no actual fire? It says "危害公共安全". The act of lighting gas could be considered dangerous method. So likely "放火". The examples: "放火" used for arson causing property loss. Here no loss, but still attempt. I'd answer "放火". Possibly also "非法持有、使用危险物品"? Not in examples.

Thus final answer: [罪名]放火<eoa>
